question: Find me consumer staples in Asia that are cheaper than their sector peers on P/E but still growing earnings — I do not want a cheap company that is cheap because it is shrinking.

tools_called.note: below_average (cohort P/E) + consecutive_growth (earnings up every year)
below_average benchmarks against the screened cohort = Asian staples; 3y consecutive earnings growth is the anti-value-trap guard

_conventions._note: For the fields below, read the `definition` and/or `sign` before interpreting the value — a negative can MEAN something (an outflow, a benefit) and an ambiguous name needs its definition. Every other field is a plain magnitude.

eps_diluted.definition: PER SHARE, in the company's REPORTING currency (NOT USD-normalized like the _usd fields) — don't mix it with the USD amounts.

answer_to_user: Screening Asian consumer-staples (980-name cohort), I required BOTH cheap-vs-peers AND growing earnings so you dont buy a shrinking value trap: P/E below the sector average (cohort average P/E = ~17.1x) AND net income up in each of the last 3 years. 80 names qualify. The cheapest ones that are ALSO consistently growing earnings: Kameda Seika (2220.JP) at 3.5x P/E, Nongshim Holdings (072710.KO) 3.6x, KC Feed (025880.KQ) 3.9x, Fujing Holdings (2497.HK) 4.1x, OUG Holdings (8041.JP) 4.5x, Ensuiko Sugar (2112.JP) 4.6x, Chuo Gyorui (8030.JP) 5.1x, China Ludao Technology (2023.HK) 6.0x, and Lam Soon Thailand (LST.BK) 6.8x — all trading at roughly a fifth-to-a-third of the ~17x sector average while still growing profits every year. The 3-year earnings-growth gate is what filters out the classic "cheap because its declining" trap; each name here has rising, not falling, earnings.
